title: Data engineering consulting: what should you walk away with?
description: Data engineering as step one of AI for firms of 40 to 500 staff. What to fix first, which warehouse fits, what it costs and what fails.
verdict: Fix the data for one named AI use, not all of it. Gartner says readiness depends on the use.[^4][^5]
Try what you own first: Business Central ships Power BI apps, and Fabric mirrors its tables without a pipeline build.[^15][^20]
Pick the warehouse by your systems: Fabric's fixed capacity suits Microsoft shops, and Snowflake bills only while a warehouse runs.[^17][^33]
Give data quality a written owner. Middle-market executives name it the top AI blocker, ahead of security.[^11][^12]
Cap spend on day one. Snowflake warns of runaway costs, and Fabric bills overage at three times the normal rate.[^33][^22]

headings.what-it-is: What is data engineering consulting, and what does it change?
headings.faq: Questions buyers ask about data engineering consulting

summary: Data engineering consulting builds the pipes, checks and data models that turn your system records into reliable data for reports and AI.[^1][^2] One RAND interviewee put data work at 80 percent of AI.[^3] Fitting the data to one named AI use makes or breaks it.[^4][^5]
walkAway: One named AI use, with the fields it needs listed and each one's owner. Gartner's first step is to align data to the use case.[^5][^13]
One subject area live and used, such as orders or invoices, not a full platform plan. Kimball and Microsoft both say build in increments, most important first.[^6][^7]
Written data tests and freshness rules your team can run, such as no blank customer IDs and no duplicate invoices.[^8][^9]
A data-quality score before and after the work. Among middle-market executives whose AI pilots had moderate or limited success, 53% blamed data quality.[^10][^12]
A monthly spend cap in the warehouse, with alerts set before anyone runs a query.[^34][^33]

spokes.why: Reports in a business intelligence (BI) tool are the first use of clean data. Business Central, for one, ships ready-made Power BI apps.[^15]
Connects AI to your ERP and CRM once the data underneath is clean. Legacy integration is a top AI blocker for middle-market executives.[^11]
Sets who owns which data and who may see it. About two-thirds of middle-market firms set AI governance before pilots.[^10]
Builds forecasts and scoring models on top, once the data has tests and an owner.[^3]
Picks the one AI use first, because Gartner says data readiness depends on the use.[^4]
Weighs a full-time hire against outside help. Database architects earned a median $139,500 a year in May 2025.[^30]

humanRole: The business owner of each data set signs off its definitions: the controller for finance data, the ops lead for orders. Gartner names lack of ownership as a common data quality challenge.[^12][^13]
A named data steward fixes what the automated checks flag. The checks do the first pass; the steward decides each fix.[^13][^8]
Business users accept each release before the old report is switched off. Kimball calls business acceptance of each deliverable the overarching goal.[^14]
The COO picks the problem and stays with it. RAND tells leaders to commit to a problem for at least a year.[^3]

recipes.name: 1. Stay on the ERP and clean the data (about 40 to 100 staff, one main system)
recipes.when: Pick this when one ERP (enterprise resource planning system) holds most of the data and the AI use needs standard fields. Ready-made ERP reports avoid a pipeline build.[^15][^16]
flow: COO: name the AI use and the report behind it
Controller: list the critical fields and who owns each
Data steward: run tests for blanks and duplicates on those fields
Analyst: install the ERP's ready-made Power BI apps or analytics add-on
Ops lead: try the AI use in one team, then retire the spreadsheet exports once the numbers match
recipes.cost: Business Central's Power BI apps need a Power BI Pro licence per user, or a Power BI or Fabric Premium capacity.[^15] NetSuite publishes no price and quotes each deal; a small Fabric capacity, the nearest public figure, is about $263 a month by our math.[^16][^17]

recipes.name: 2. Microsoft shop with a small Fabric capacity (about 100 to 300 staff)
recipes.when: Pick this when your data sits in Business Central, Dynamics 365 or other Microsoft tools. Fabric can keep a live copy of those tables with no ETL (extract, transform and load) code to write.[^20][^21]
flow: IT lead: set who can see which tables before anything is copied
Data engineer: mirror the ERP tables into Fabric
Data engineer: model the most important subject area first
Controller: reconcile totals to the books
COO: approve the first AI use on the new store
recipes.cost: Fabric bills $0.18 per capacity-unit (CU) hour, so the smallest F2 size runs $262.80 a month pay-as-you-go by our math.[^17] A one-year reservation ($938 per CU) cuts F2 to about $156 a month by our math; mirroring's copy compute is free.[^18][^19]

recipes.name: 3. Several systems, not all Microsoft (about 150 to 500 staff)
recipes.when: Pick this when the ERP, CRM (customer relationship management) and other tools disagree and none of them is Microsoft's. Snowflake bills only while a warehouse runs, and BigQuery by the data each query scans.[^33][^27]
flow: COO: pick the AI use and its two or three source systems
IT lead: set who can see which data before anything is copied
Data engineer: connect each source with a managed connector tool, such as Fivetran
Data engineer: shrink the warehouse size and set a spend cap
Data steward: write tests for each critical field
Division head: accept the first subject area
recipes.cost: A Snowflake X-Small warehouse costs $2.00 an hour while it runs on Standard, and a Databricks 2X-Small serverless one $2.80, by our math.[^23][^24][^25] Fivetran's own Standard-plan example for a firm of 1-200 employees totals $511.15 a month.[^28]

ownData.title: Which data tools do firms your size hire for?
ownData.intro: We counted 5,784 US Data & Analytics ads at those firms and 7,090 at firms of 501 to 5,000 staff, on 28 Nov 2026.[^31] More than half of ads at both sizes ask for data quality skills, by our count.[^31]
ownData.note: Method: US job ads in the JobsPipe index, posted in the 30 days to 28 Nov 2026, job function Data & Analytics, by employer size. A term counts when the ad's title or description names it; shares are our math, and the index flags counts as approximate. Limits: one ad can name several tools, reposts and agency ads are included, and an ad shows what firms hire for, not what they run.

watchOuts: The data doesn't fit the use. RAND names missing data as a root cause of AI failure, so map the use's fields before any build.[^3][^4]
Gartner predicts organizations will abandon 60% of AI projects that lack AI-ready data. Test the data against the one use before money goes into models.[^5]
A big-bang build that ships nothing for months. Kimball warns against it; ship one subject area, then the next.[^6][^7]
Runaway compute. A new Databricks SQL warehouse defaults to X-Large, and Snowflake warehouses without monitors risk runaway costs, so size down and cap spend on day one.[^26][^33]
Pipelines break and nobody owns the fix. In a Fivetran vendor survey of 500 leaders at firms over 5,000 staff, pipelines failed 4.7 times a month, each fix taking nearly 13 hours.[^29]
Wrong numbers reach people unless tests catch them first. In a dbt Labs vendor survey of 363 data practitioners and leaders, 71% named that a top concern.[^32][^8]
howToTest: Ask them to start from one named AI use. Gartner says data readiness depends on the use, so an advisor who starts with all your data is guessing.[^4]
Have them size the build per source system. TDWI's ballpark scores each system 3, 9 or 15 worker-days, plus a margin for uncertainty.[^35]
Agree the two or three quality measures that matter for the use, and score them before work starts. Gartner advises picking two or three per use.[^12][^36]
Ask for written tests on each critical field: not blank, unique, from an allowed list, and matching a real record elsewhere.[^8]
Check that each data feed arrived on time, at least twice as often as reports need it: every 12 hours for a daily report.[^9]
Test any AI output on a realistic sample of your own records, not a demo set.[^37]
Run the old report and the new one side by side, and switch only when the totals match. Databricks, a vendor, advises running benchmark queries alongside legacy systems before cutover.[^38]

Ask for a handover: written notes on each data set, who fixes a broken feed, and every account in your firm's name. RAND warns that without notes, losing a data engineer can leave no one knowing which data sets are reliable.[^3]
Price the result: hours a month spent fixing broken data feeds today, times what an hour of that person's time costs you.[^29]

faq.q: Do we need a data warehouse before we start AI?
faq.a: No, because readiness depends on the AI use, not on owning a warehouse.[^4] Business Central, for one, ships ready-made Power BI apps that report without a separate warehouse.[^15]

faq.q: Should a firm our size pick Fabric or Snowflake?
faq.a: Pick Fabric if you run Microsoft systems, because it mirrors Business Central and Dataverse with no pipeline code.[^20][^21] Fabric bills a fixed capacity from $0.18 per CU hour; Snowflake bills $2.00 per credit while a warehouse runs.[^17][^23] By our count, Snowflake shows up in 16.1% of data job ads at firms your size and Fabric in 4.7%.[^31]

faq.q: What does the data software cost a month?
faq.a: A small Fabric capacity runs about $263 a month by our math, pay-as-you-go.[^17] A Snowflake X-Small warehouse costs $2.00 an hour while it runs, and BigQuery's first 1 TiB (tebibyte) of queries a month is free.[^23][^27]

faq.q: How long does a data engineering project take?
faq.a: No neutral study gives a week count, so plan in increments, with the most important subject area first.[^7][^6] Databricks, a vendor, says a proof of concept takes weeks and a production pilot several months.[^38]

faq.q: Can we report straight from the ERP?
faq.a: Yes, for standard reports: Business Central ships Power BI apps for finance, sales and inventory.[^15] For more, mirror up to 1,000 Business Central tables into Fabric, a feature still in preview.[^20]

faq.q: Should we hire a data engineer instead?
faq.a: Only when the work will fill a full-time role for years. For comparison, database architects earned a median $139,500 in May 2025.[^30] By our count, 41 data and analytics ads at 40-500 staff firms posted a median pay midpoint of $131,500; only 9 data-engineer ads posted pay.[^31]

pickElse: Your reports come from one ERP and the questions are standard: install Business Central's ready-made Power BI apps instead.[^15]
Your data already sits in Dataverse or Business Central: use Link to Fabric or mirroring, which need no pipeline build.[^21][^19]
Your data is small and queried now and then: BigQuery's first 1 TiB of queries a month is free.[^27] Fivetran's free plan moves up to 500,000 monthly active rows.[^28]
No one can commit to one problem for a year: wait. RAND tells leaders to stay with a problem at least that long.[^3]

sources.name: UK Government Digital, Data and Technology Capability Framework, Data engineer role
sources.what: UK government role definition: a data engineer develops and constructs data products and services, and integrates them into systems and business processes. The role implements data flows, re-engineers manual data flows and writes extract, transform and load (ETL) code.

sources.name: Snowflake, What is data engineering (vendor)
sources.what: Vendor definition (Snowflake's): data engineering is the discipline of building and maintaining the infrastructure, processing logic and data models that turn source information into reliable, accessible data for business applications, analytics and AI systems.

sources.name: RAND, The Root Causes of Failure for Artificial Intelligence Projects and How They Can Succeed (RR-A2680-1, 13 Aug 2024)
sources.what: Interviews with 65 data scientists and engineers (50 industry, 15 academic). By some estimates, more than 80 percent of AI projects fail, twice the rate of IT projects that don't involve AI. An interviewee: "80 percent of AI is the dirty work of data engineering." Two of five root causes: lacking the necessary data, and inadequate infrastructure to manage data and deploy models. 30 of 50 industry interviewees discussed persistent data quality issues. Leaders should be prepared to commit each product team to solving a specific problem for at least a year. Without documentation, the loss of a data engineer might mean no one knows which datasets are reliable.

sources.name: Gartner, AI-ready data
sources.what: There is no way to make data AI-ready in general or in advance; readiness depends on the AI use case.

sources.name: Gartner press release, Lack of AI-Ready Data Puts AI Projects at Risk (26 Feb 2025)
sources.what: Survey of 1,203 data management leaders, July 2024: 63% of organizations either do not have or are unsure if they have the right data management practices for AI. Gartner predicts that through 2026 organizations will abandon 60% of AI projects unsupported by AI-ready data. Steps: align data to the use case, meet governance requirements, use active metadata, prepare data pipelines, and assure and enhance the data.

sources.name: Kimball Group, DW/BI lifecycle method
sources.what: Iteratively develop the data warehouse in manageable lifecycle increments rather than attempting a galactic Big Bang.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Dimensional modeling in Fabric Data Warehouse
sources.what: Build out your enterprise data warehouse iteratively. Start with the most important subject areas first.

sources.name: dbt Developer Hub, About data tests property
sources.what: dbt ships four generic data tests: not_null, unique, accepted_values and relationships (referential integrity).

sources.name: dbt Developer Hub, Source freshness
sources.what: Freshness checks use warn_after and error_after thresholds. Run them at least double the frequency of your lowest service-level agreement (SLA): a 1-day SLA is checked every 12 hours.

sources.name: RSM US Middle Market AI Survey 2026, report (21 Jul 2026)
sources.what: Survey of 1,030 middle-market executives (827 US, 203 Canada), 5-16 Mar 2026; middle market means $30M-$10B revenue. Of middle-market firms whose AI pilots had moderate or limited success, 53% blamed data quality and 47% integration. About two-thirds (67%) of respondents establish AI governance controls before implementing pilots or production.

sources.name: RSM US Middle Market AI Survey 2026
sources.what: Survey of 1,030 middle-market executives (827 US, 203 Canada): 34% cited data quality as a top barrier to AI deployment, followed by security and privacy concerns (30%) and legacy systems integration (28%). Read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Gartner, Data quality: why it matters and how to achieve it
sources.what: Lack of ownership is a data quality challenge: business leaders agree data quality matters but do not view it as their responsibility. Pick the two or three data quality metrics most important for the use case to measure and improve. Gartner surveys: 59% of organizations do not measure data quality.

sources.name: DAMA-NL, Data Quality Management System Framework (2024, v12)
sources.what: Trade body framework. Roles related to data quality are defined, such as data owner (accountable), data steward (responsible), data custodian, data quality analyst, data supplier and data user.

sources.name: Kimball Group, Design Tip #115: Kimball Lifecycle in a Nutshell
sources.what: Requirements start from what business users do; the overarching goal should be business acceptance of the DW/BI deliverables; develop in manageable lifecycle increments rather than a Big Bang deliverable.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Install Business Central Power BI apps
sources.what: Business Central ships Power BI apps (finance, sales, inventory and others) that install as connectors. They need a Power BI Pro licence per user, or Power BI or Microsoft Fabric Premium capacity.

sources.name: NetSuite, Data Intelligence (formerly NetSuite Analytics Warehouse)
sources.what: NetSuite Data Intelligence is available as an add-on module, with a prebuilt pipeline from NetSuite. NetSuite is sold on an annual licence; no price on the page, read 28 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Microsoft Azure Retail Prices API, Fabric Capacity, East US

sources.name: Microsoft Azure Retail Prices API, Fabric Capacity Reservation, East US
sources.what: Read live 28 Nov 2026: Fabric Capacity Reservation, 1 Year term, $938 per CU; 3 Years term $2,814 per CU.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Mirroring in Fabric overview
sources.what: Background Fabric compute used to replicate data into OneLake is free and doesn't consume capacity; querying mirrored data is charged at regular rates; a running Fabric capacity is required.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Business Central and Fabric
sources.what: Prerelease documentation: Business Central data mirroring to Fabric is planned as a production-ready preview from October 2026, with up to 1,000 selected tables, an initial snapshot and incremental sync.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Link your Dataverse environment to Microsoft Fabric
sources.what: Link to Fabric makes Dataverse data (Dynamics 365 and Power Apps) available in OneLake through shortcuts, with no ETL to build.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn, Fabric throttling policy
sources.what: Fabric delays interactive work after 10 minutes of overuse, rejects interactive requests after 60 minutes, and rejects background jobs after 24 hours. Overage is billed at three times the normal rate.

sources.what: Vendor claim (Databricks): a proof of concept takes weeks and a production pilot takes several months. Validate by running benchmark queries alongside legacy systems before rollout.

answers.walk-away: Walk away with one AI use and its fields mapped, one subject area live, written data tests, a before-and-after quality score and a spend cap.[^5][^6][^8]
answers.spokes: Most firms need data cleanup first, then reports, AI connections to the ERP and CRM, and models, in that order, because data quality is the top AI blocker.[^11][^4]
answers.human-role: Business owners sign off each data set's definitions, a data steward decides each fix the checks flag, and business users accept each release.[^12][^13][^14]
answers.recipes: Stay on the ERP when one system holds the data, add a small Fabric capacity in a Microsoft shop, or use a pay-per-use warehouse across mixed systems.[^15][^17][^23]
answers.own-data: Firms of 40 to 500 staff name Snowflake in 16.1% of data job ads and Microsoft Fabric in 4.7%, by our count of US ads on 28 Nov 2026.[^31]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI pilots stall when the data doesn't fit the use, the build tries everything at once, compute runs uncapped, or nobody owns broken pipelines.[^3][^6][^33]
answers.benchmark: Judge an advisor by whether they start from one AI use, size the build per source system, score data quality first and run old and new reports side by side.[^4][^35][^12]
answers.something-else: Skip outside help when your ERP's own reports cover the questions, your Microsoft data can be mirrored, or volumes fit a free tier.[^15][^19][^27]

offer.heading: Not sure what to fix first?
offer.body: Fix the data behind one AI use first, such as the order or invoice records it will read. In a free 30-minute call, bring that report and leave with the fields it needs, the first fix and a number to beat.

reviews.notes: Dana got what to fix first (one AI use, its fields, an owner), which build fits, and outside software costs. Asked how long: no neutral week count exists in the research, so the FAQ says so, gives the build-in-increments rule and labels the Databricks timeline as the vendor's. The pay FAQ used 'median midpoint' with only the thin 9-ad figure; it now leads with the 41-ad data and analytics figure and flags the 9-ad sample as thin.

Stalled on mirroring, freshness checks and managed connector tool. Mirroring now reads 'keep a live copy of those tables', freshness reads 'check that each data feed arrived on time', and the connector step names Fivetran as the example. ETL, ERP, CRM, BI, CU and TiB are spelled out on first use.

Wanted to try it in one unit before a firm-wide change. The small-firm build now has the ops lead try the AI use in one team before retiring spreadsheet exports. Price-the-result step turns hours spent fixing broken feeds into dollars; no sourced margin figure for a firm this size is in the research, so none is given.

Read as head of IT. Access control was only in the Microsoft build; the mixed-systems build now starts with the IT lead setting who can see which data. Asked who keeps it running after the consultants leave: added a handover test (notes on each data set, who fixes a broken feed, accounts in the firm's name), backed by RAND on knowledge leaving with engineers.

Steve got the answer in 10 seconds from the bottom line: fix data for one use, try what you own, cap spend. Cost of the software is shown from vendor list prices, labelled by our math where we multiplied. No Zavient price, per Russell's rule. No consulting firms named. Risk (runaway compute, broken pipelines) and who signs off are clear.
